name: agent
description: The box: the fixed in-container phase order context -> prelude -> agent -> postlude -> result. Deterministic, engine-owned sequencing around user-filled phases — opaque context/prelude hooks, unrestricted agent invocation inside the sealed environment, and structured result extraction and validation at the container boundary.

requirements.title: Fixed box phase order
requirements.description: Every agent step executes the same internal sequence: environment setup (an agent-specific skills-link phase when the template declares one, delegated credentials, remote host-key policy, repo clone from the gateway when a repo param is present, signing config derived from the forwarded agent socket), then the context and prelude hooks, then the agent (skippable by the prelude on a template that declares agent_optional — the phase stays in the order as a logged no-op), then the optional postlude hook, then result emission and verification. After each user-filled phase that exits 0 the sequencer honors a halt request (halt.json in the result directory), emitting a halted attempt record and running no later phase. The order is engine-owned and not configurable; there is no in-container DAG.

requirements.title: Deterministic prelude contract
requirements.description: context and prelude are opaque user scripts run deterministically (no agent, no credentials beyond the delegated handles) before the agent starts. Contract: they receive the step's typed inputs as environment, must produce the context bundle (a prompt-body document plus optional machine-readable sidecars) in a well-known directory, and must exit 0. A failed or bundle-less prelude aborts the step with a structured handoff record — the agent never starts.

requirements.title: Unrestricted agent invocation
requirements.description: The agent phase invokes the configured agent skill headlessly with full permission bypass inside the box; the sealed environment (pinned toolset, egress lock, single-role key, gateway-only remote) is the restriction — there is no second in-container permission gate. The invocation's shape is data: a concrete invocation profile (FABER_INVOKE_PROFILE, compiled by config; absent ⇒ the anonymous built-in default reproducing the historical dialect byte-for-byte) drives a pure expander over subcommand, prompt/skill placement, fixed flags, and the model/effort/budget flag names — no vendor literal in the engine. The invocation passes the skill name, the context bundle as prompt body, the model and effort level (mandatory per-template config, passed through opaquely), optional extra instruction, and optional budget bound from config. On a template declaring agent_optional, a prelude that wrote FABER_SKIP_AGENT=1 into bundle.env skips the invocation entirely (logged no-op; the record marks agent_skipped; the output contract still holds); a template without the opt-in ignores the signal with a warning.

requirements.title: Structured result extraction
requirements.description: The step's result is a typed record read from a well-known result file in the mounted result directory, schema-validated against the template's declared output before it is threaded to any downstream step. A missing result file after an otherwise-successful agent phase yields a minimal engine-written fallback record; verification hooks (e.g. confirming a declared side-effect exists) run after extraction. A halted record bypasses extraction and verification (nothing threads; the halt arm must carry a reason or the record fails halt-invalid).

requirements.title: Deferred: non-JSON artifacts
requirements.description: Backlog (design edge case 3): inter-step artifacts beyond typed JSON — large files, research outputs, deliverables that belong to no git repo. Needs an artifact store or pass-by-reference convention in the result contract. First pass supports only typed JSON outputs plus repo state behind the gateway.

requirements.title: Deferred: generic context resolvers
requirements.description: Backlog (design edge case 4): richer context gathering (resolve a work item to its authoritative documents) without faber learning the user's spec or tracker tooling — likely a declared resolve_context command contract mirroring the data-source contract. First pass: the context hook is a single opaque script.

components.name: PhaseSequencer
components.description: The in-container entry program that owns the fixed phase order: chowns the writable mounts (including the /run/secrets tmpfs when present) and drops to the run user, validates the step's env contract, materializes file-mode secrets from the stdin payload into /run/secrets and exports them to env, applies host-key policy, clones from the gateway remote, configures commit signing from the forwarded agent, then drives context -> prelude -> agent -> postlude -> result with fail-stop between phases and a post-phase halt-request check (halt.json -> a halted attempt record) after each user-filled phase.

components.name: PreludeHooks
components.description: The context/prelude/postlude hook contract: input environment, the context-bundle output convention, exit-code semantics, the halt.json operator-stop request, and the structured handoff record written when a hook fails. Owns the deferred context-resolver seam.

components.name: AgentInvoker
components.description: The agent phase: a pure expander over the concrete invocation profile (FABER_INVOKE_PROFILE; absent ⇒ built-in default) that assembles the headless invocation (skill, context bundle, model, effort, extra instruction, budget bound — placed per the profile's dialect), executes it, and maps its exit status into the phase flow. Owns the prelude-driven skip: FABER_SKIP_AGENT=1 in bundle.env on an agent_optional template makes the phase a logged no-op with the record marked agent_skipped.

components.name: ResultExtractor
components.description: Reads the result file from the result directory, validates it against the template's output schema, writes the fallback record when absent, runs post-result verification, and passes a halted record through unextracted (payload dropped, halt reason asserted host-side). Owns the deferred non-JSON artifact seam. Owns the faber↔faber-box result-contract schema version (contract: 1), stamped into the box env and into result.json and asserted host-side on extract — a mismatch detects a stale or foreign box binary (host-config `box_bin`), never a migration path.

data_flows.name: Box execution flow
data_flows.description: Step env contract (inputs, bindings, handles) -> deterministic setup -> context/prelude hooks (context bundle) -> agent invocation (repo mutations via gateway, result file) -> optional postlude hook (deterministic post-agent work over the agent's artifacts) -> result extraction + schema validation -> typed result record to the host.
